# mcgf

The goal of `mcgf` is to provide easy-to-use functions for simulating
and fitting covariance models. It provides functions for simulating
(regime-switching) Markov chain Gaussian fields with covariance
functions of the Gneiting class by simple kriging. Parameter estimation
methods such as weighted least squares and maximum likelihood estimation
are available. Below is an example of simulating an MCGF and estimating
its parameters for an MCGF.

## Installation

You can install the development version of mcgf from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("tianxia-jia/mcgf")
```

## Data Simulation

To simulate an MCGF with fully symmetric covariance structure, we begin
with simulating 10 locations randomly.

``` r

library(mcgf)
set.seed(123)
h <- rdists(10)
```

Next, we simulate an MCGF with the general stationary covariance
structure. In this example the covariance structure is a convex
combination of a base separable model and a Lagrangian model that
accounts for asymmetry.

``` r

N <- 1000
lag <- 5

par_base <- list(
    par_s = list(nugget = 0, c = 0.001, gamma = 0.5),
    par_t = list(a = 0.5, alpha = 0.8)
)
par_lagr <- list(v1 = 200, v2 = 200, k = 2)

sim1 <- mcgf_sim(
    N = N,
    base = "sep",
    lagrangian = "lagr_tri",
    par_base = par_base,
    par_lagr = par_lagr,
    lambda = 0.2,
    dists = h,
    lag = lag
)
sim1 <- sim1[-c(1:(lag + 1)), ]
rownames(sim1) <- 1:nrow(sim1)

sim1 <- list(data = sim1, dists = h)
```

## Parameter Estimation

### Create an `mcgf` object

To estimate parameters, we need to calculate auto-correlations and
cross-correlations. Let’s first create an `mcgf` object. The `mcgf`
class extends the `data.frame` with more attributes.

``` r

sim1_mcgf <- mcgf(sim1$data, dists = sim1$dists)
#> `time` is not provided, assuming rows are equally spaced temporally.
```

Then the acfs and ccfs can be added to this object as follows.

``` r

sim1_mcgf <- add_acfs(sim1_mcgf, lag_max = lag)
sim1_mcgf <- add_ccfs(sim1_mcgf, lag_max = lag)
```

### Estimate base model

To perform parameter estimation, we can start with estimating the
parameters for spatial and temporal models.

``` r

fit_spatial <- fit_base(
    sim1_mcgf,
    model = "spatial",
    lag = lag,
    par_init = c(c = 0.001, gamma = 0.5),
    par_fixed = c(nugget = 0)
)
fit_spatial$fit
#> $par
#>           c       gamma 
#> 0.001160802 0.500000000 
#> 
#> $objective
#> [1] 1.640593
#> 
#> $convergence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $evaluations
#> function gradient 
#>       21       20 
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] "both X-convergence and relative convergence (5)"
```

``` r

fit_temporal <- fit_base(
    sim1_mcgf,
    model = "temporal",
    lag = lag,
    par_init = c(a = 0.3, alpha = 0.5)
)
fit_temporal$fit
#> $par
#>         a     alpha 
#> 0.6528906 0.7560970 
#> 
#> $objective
#> [1] 0.004306706
#> 
#> $convergence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 18
#> 
#> $evaluations
#> function gradient 
#>       23       43 
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] "relative convergence (4)"
```

Alternatively, we can fit the separable model all at once:

``` r

fit_sep <- fit_base(
    sim1_mcgf,
    model = "sep",
    lag = lag,
    par_init = c(
        c = 0.001,
        gamma = 0.5,
        a = 0.5,
        alpha = 0.5
    ),
    par_fixed = c(nugget = 0)
)
fit_sep$fit
#> $par
#>           c       gamma           a       alpha 
#> 0.001154864 0.500000000 0.624551338 0.735490605 
#> 
#> $objective
#> [1] 3.488305
#> 
#> $convergence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 18
#> 
#> $evaluations
#> function gradient 
#>       49       88 
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] "relative convergence (4)"
```

we can also estimate the parameters using MLE:

``` r

fit_sep2 <- fit_base(
    sim1_mcgf,
    model = "sep",
    lag = lag,
    par_init = c(
        c = 0.001,
        gamma = 0.5,
        a = 0.5,
        alpha = 0.5
    ),
    par_fixed = c(nugget = 0),
    method = "mle",
)
fit_sep2$fit
#> $par
#>           c       gamma           a       alpha 
#> 0.001197799 0.500000000 0.804621207 1.000000000 
#> 
#> $objective
#> [1] -11520.04
#> 
#> $convergence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 17
#> 
#> $evaluations
#> function gradient 
#>       55       78 
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] "relative convergence (4)"
```

Now we will add the base model to `x_mcgf`:

``` r

sim1_mcgf <- add_base(sim1_mcgf, fit_base = fit_sep)
```

To print the current model, we do

``` r

model(sim1_mcgf)
#> ----------------------------------------
#>                  Model
#> ----------------------------------------
#> - Time lag: 5 
#> - Scale of time lag: 1 
#> - Forecast horizon: 1 
#> ----------------------------------------
#>                  Base
#> ----------------------------------------
#> - Base model: sep 
#> - Parameters:
#>           c       gamma           a       alpha      nugget 
#> 0.001154864 0.500000000 0.624551338 0.735490605 0.000000000 
#> 
#> - Fixed parameters:
#> nugget 
#>      0 
#> 
#> - Parameter estimation method: wls 
#> 
#> - Optimization function: nlminb 
#> ----------------------------------------
#>               Lagrangian
#> ----------------------------------------
#> - Lagrangian model: 
#> - Parameters:
#> NULL
#> 
#> - Fixed parameters:
#> NULL
#> 
#> - Parameter estimation method: 
#> 
#> - Optimization function:
```

### Estimate the Lagrangian model

Similarly, we can estimate the parameters for the Lagrangian component
by

``` r

fit_lagr <- fit_lagr(
    sim1_mcgf,
    model = "lagr_tri",
    par_init = c(v1 = 300, v2 = 300, lambda = 0.15),
    par_fixed = c(k = 2)
)
fit_lagr$fit
#> $par
#>      lambda          v1          v2 
#>   0.1757035 232.0852117 203.8869305 
#> 
#> $objective
#> [1] 1.627017
#> 
#> $convergence
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 32
#> 
#> $evaluations
#> function gradient 
#>       35      126 
#> 
#> $message
#> [1] "relative convergence (4)"
```

We can add the Lagrangian model by

``` r

sim1_mcgf <- add_lagr(sim1_mcgf, fit_lagr = fit_lagr)
```

Finally we may print the final model:

``` r

model(sim1_mcgf)
#> ----------------------------------------
#>                  Model
#> ----------------------------------------
#> - Time lag: 5 
#> - Scale of time lag: 1 
#> - Forecast horizon: 1 
#> ----------------------------------------
#>                  Base
#> ----------------------------------------
#> - Base model: sep 
#> - Parameters:
#>           c       gamma           a       alpha      nugget 
#> 0.001154864 0.500000000 0.624551338 0.735490605 0.000000000 
#> 
#> - Fixed parameters:
#> nugget 
#>      0 
#> 
#> - Parameter estimation method: wls 
#> 
#> - Optimization function: nlminb 
#> ----------------------------------------
#>               Lagrangian
#> ----------------------------------------
#> - Lagrangian model: lagr_tri 
#> - Parameters:
#>      lambda          v1          v2           k 
#>   0.1757035 232.0852117 203.8869305   2.0000000 
#> 
#> - Fixed parameters:
#> k 
#> 2 
#> 
#> - Parameter estimation method: wls 
#> 
#> - Optimization function: nlminb
```

### Kriging forecast

This package provides kriging forecasts (and intervals) for empirical,
base, and general stationary models.

``` r

# Empirical model
fit_emp <-
    krige(sim1_mcgf,
        model = "empirical",
        interval = TRUE
    )
rmse_emp <- sqrt(mean(colMeans((sim1_mcgf - fit_emp$fit)^2, na.rm = T)))

# Base separable model
fit_base <-
    krige(sim1_mcgf,
        model = "base",
        interval = TRUE
    )
rmse_base <-
    sqrt(mean(colMeans((sim1_mcgf - fit_base$fit)^2, na.rm = T)))

# Stationary model
fit_stat <-
    krige(sim1_mcgf,
        model = "all",
        interval = TRUE
    )
rmse_stat <-
    sqrt(mean(colMeans((sim1_mcgf - fit_stat$fit)^2, na.rm = T)))

rmse <- c(rmse_emp, rmse_base, rmse_stat)
names(rmse) <- c("Empirical", "Separable", "Stationary")
rmse
#>  Empirical  Separable Stationary 
#>  0.7212175  0.7685016  0.7355458
```

# Package index

## All functions

- [`acf_rs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/acf_rs.md) :
  Calculate regime-switching auto-correlation

- [`acfs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/acfs.md) :
  Generic function for calculating autocorrelation

- [`acfs(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/acfs.mcgf.md)
  [`acfs(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/acfs.mcgf.md)
  [`` `acfs<-`() ``](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/acfs.mcgf.md)
  [`add_acfs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/acfs.mcgf.md)
  :

  Extract, calculate, or assign mean auto-correlations for an `mcgf` or
  `mcgf_rs` object

- [`add_base()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_base.md)
  : Generic function for adding a base model

- [`add_base(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_base.mcgf.md)
  [`` `base<-`() ``](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_base.mcgf.md)
  :

  Add base model outputted from
  [`fit_base()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_base.md)
  to an `mcgf` object.

- [`add_base(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_base.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Add base model outputted from
  [`fit_base()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_base.md)
  to an `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`add_lagr()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_lagr.md)
  : Generic function for adding a Lagrangian model

- [`add_lagr(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_lagr.mcgf.md)
  [`` `lagr<-`() ``](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_lagr.mcgf.md)
  :

  Add lagr model outputted from
  [`fit_lagr()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_lagr.md)
  to a `mcgf` object.

- [`add_lagr(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/add_lagr.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Add lagr model outputted from
  [`fit_lagr()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_lagr.md)
  to a `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`ccf_rs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccf_rs.md) :
  Calculate regime-switching cross-correlation

- [`ccfs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccfs.md) :
  Generic function for calculating cross-correlation

- [`ccfs(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccfs.mcgf.md)
  [`ccfs(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccfs.mcgf.md)
  [`` `ccfs<-`() ``](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccfs.mcgf.md)
  [`add_ccfs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccfs.mcgf.md)
  :

  Extract, calculate, or assign cross-correlations for an `mcgf` or
  `mcgf_rs` object

- [`ccov()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccov.md) :
  Generic functions for calculating joint covariance/correlation matrix
  for mcgf objects

- [`ccov(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccov.mcgf.md)
  :

  Covariance/correlation for joint distribution of an `mcgf` object

- [`ccov(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/ccov.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Covariance/correlation for joint distribution of an `mcgf_rs`object

- [`cor2cov()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor2cov.md)
  [`cor2cov_ar()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor2cov.md)
  : Convert correlation to covariance

- [`cor_cauchy()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_cauchy.md)
  : Calculate Cauchy correlation

- [`cor_exp()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_exp.md)
  : Calculate exponential correlation

- [`cor_fs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_fs.md) :
  Calculate correlation for fully symmetric model

- [`cor_lagr_askey()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_lagr_askey.md)
  : Calculate Lagrangian correlation of the Askey form

- [`cor_lagr_exp()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_lagr_exp.md)
  : Calculate Lagrangian correlation of the exponential form

- [`cor_lagr_tri()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_lagr_tri.md)
  : Calculate Lagrangian correlation of the triangular form

- [`cor_sep()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_sep.md)
  : Calculate correlation for separable model

- [`cor_stat()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_stat.md)
  : Calculate general stationary correlation.

- [`cor_stat_rs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/cor_stat_rs.md)
  : Calculate general stationary correlation.

- [`dists()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/dists.md) :
  Generic function for calculating distance matrices

- [`dists(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/dists.mcgf.md)
  [`` `dists<-`() ``](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/dists.mcgf.md)
  :

  Calculating distance matrices for an `mcgf` object

- [`find_dists()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/find_dists.md)
  : Calculate (signed) distances between coordinates

- [`find_dists_new()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/find_dists_new.md)
  : Calculate (signed) distances between coordinates

- [`fit_base()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_base.md)
  : Fit correlation base models

- [`fit_base(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_base.mcgf.md)
  :

  Parameter estimation for symmetric correlation functions for an `mcgf`
  object.

- [`fit_base(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_base.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Parameter estimation for symmetric correlation functions for an
  `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`fit_lagr()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_lagr.md)
  : Fit correlation Lagrangian models

- [`fit_lagr(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_lagr.mcgf.md)
  :

  Parameter estimation for Lagrangian correlation functions for an
  `mcgf` object.

- [`fit_lagr(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/fit_lagr.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Parameter estimation for Lagrangian correlation functions for an
  `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`is.mcgf()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/is.mcgf.md)
  :

  Check if an object is an `mcgf` object.

- [`is.mcgf_rs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/is.mcgf_rs.md)
  [`as.mcgf_rs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/is.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Check if an object is an `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`krige()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/krige.md) :
  Generic function for computing kriging forecasts

- [`krige(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/krige.mcgf.md)
  :

  Obtain kriging forecasts for an `mcgf` object.

- [`krige(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/krige.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Obtain kriging forecasts for an `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`krige_new()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/krige_new.md)
  : Generic function for computing kriging forecasts for new locations

- [`krige_new(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/krige_new.mcgf.md)
  :

  Obtain kriging forecasts for new locations for an `mcgf` object.

- [`krige_new(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/krige_new.mcgf_rs.md)
  :

  Obtain kriging forecasts for new locations for an `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`mcgf()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/mcgf.md) :
  Create mcgf object

- [`mcgf_rs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/mcgf_rs.md)
  : Create mcgf_rs object

- [`mcgf_rs_sim()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/mcgf_rs_sim.md)
  : Simulate regime-switching Markov chain Gaussian field

- [`mcgf_sim()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/mcgf_sim.md)
  : Simulate Markov chain Gaussian field

- [`model()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/model.md) :

  Generic function for displaying fitted models for `mcgf` objects

- [`model(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/model.mcgf.md)
  [`model(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/model.mcgf.md)
  :

  Display fitted models for an `mcgf` or `mcgf_rs` object

- [`print(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/print.mcgf.md)
  :

  Print an `mcgf` object.

- [`rdists()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/rdists.md) :
  Generate random distance matrices

- [`sd_rs()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sd_rs.md) :
  Calculate standard deviation for each location under each regime.

- [`sds()`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sds.md) :
  Generic function for standard deviations for each column

- [`sds(`*`<mcgf>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sds.mcgf.md)
  [`sds(`*`<mcgf_rs>`*`)`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sds.mcgf.md)
  [`` `sds<-`() ``](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sds.mcgf.md)
  :

  Extract, calculate, or assign standard deviations for an `mcgf` or
  `mcgf_rs` object.

- [`sim1`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sim1.md) :
  Simulated Markov chain Gaussian field

- [`sim2`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sim2.md) :
  Simulated regime-switching Markov chain Gaussian field

- [`sim3`](https://tianxia-jia.github.io/mcgf/reference/sim3.md) :
  Simulated regime-switching Markov chain Gaussian field

  Ireland wind data, 1961-1978
